encounters.cc: Exertional fatigue and intermittent chest discomfort over the past three months

lines: Exertional fatigue and intermittent chest discomfort over the past three months
A 64-year-old woman comes to the cardiology clinic for evaluation of exertional fatigue and intermittent chest discomfort over the past three months.
The discomfort is described as a vague pressure in the central chest that occurs when she walks long distances or climbs stairs and resolves with rest.
- Cervical spinal stenosis with cervical spondylotic myelopathy
She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well-controlled.
- Total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (3 months prior)
She takes with lisinopril and atorvastatin.
- Prednisone 60 mg PO daily (tapering regimen for giant cell arteritis)
She does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally.
Blood pressure today is 132/78 mmHg, and pulse is 76/min and regular.
Cardiovascular examination reveals normal heart sounds without murmurs, rubs, or gallops.
An ECG performed in the clinic is normal.

encounters.cc: Progressive difficulty reading and recognizing faces over the past several months

lines: Progressive difficulty reading and recognizing faces over the past several months

This is a 68-year-old female with established dry age-related macular degeneration who returns for reassessment of progressive visual concerns, following recent Cardiology evaluation for chest discomfort.
She states that her peripheral vision remains intact, but she finds it increasingly hard to focus on words in the center of a page.

Her condition has been slowly worsening, and she has stopped knitting, a hobby she previously enjoyed, because "the center of the pattern looks like it's missing." She denies any eye pain, redness, or flashes of light.
- Cervical spinal stenosis with cervical spondylotic myelopathy
Her past medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well-controlled with medications.
- Total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (3 months prior)
- Prednisone 60 mg PO daily (tapering regimen for giant cell arteritis)
She is a non-smoker and lives independently.
During the visit, she is asked to look at an Amsler grid, and she reports that the straight lines appear wavy and distorted in the central area.
Fundoscopy reveals multiple yellowish-white deposits clustered around the macula.
The retina surrounding the macula appears thin and mildly pigmented but without evidence of hemorrhage or neovascularization.
The image below shows the fundoscopic finding (left) and her perception of the Amsler grid test (right).

encounters.cc: Several months of progressive difficulty using hands to grasp small objects and perform fine motor tasks

lines: Several months of progressive difficulty using hands to grasp small objects and perform fine motor tasks
The patient is a 69-year-old female with established cervical spinal stenosis and cervical spondylotic myelopathy presenting with progression of upper extremity symptoms.
Her recent medical history includes management of coronary artery disease, age-related macular degeneration, and major depressive disorder.
She reports struggling to grasp small objects like keys and has recently needed assistance with tasks like buttoning her blouse and opening jars.
She denies recent trauma, falls, or fever.
Her symptoms have been slowly progressive and worse on the right.
She also describes intermittent tingling and dull aching pain that radiates down her right arm, sometimes reaching the hand.
She does not report neck stiffness, gait instability, or bowel/bladder incontinence.
- Cervical spinal stenosis with cervical spondylotic myelopathy
Her medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both controlled with medication.
- Total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (3 months prior)
- Prednisone 60 mg PO daily (tapering regimen for giant cell arteritis)
Alcohol: Occasional (1-2 glasses of wine per week).
Neurologic examination shows decreased grip strength and reduced fine motor coordination on the right.
Reflexes are symmetric, and no spasticity or hyperreflexia is observed.
There is patchy sensory loss in the right hand.

encounters.cc: Six-month history of intermittent dizziness and left arm fatigue with exertion

lines: Six-month history of intermittent dizziness and left arm fatigue with exertion
The patient is a 69-year-old female with coronary artery disease and giant cell arteritis on corticosteroids who returns for vascular evaluation after cardiology care.
She presents with a 6-month history of intermittent dizziness and left arm fatigue.
She reports these symptoms often occur after carrying groceries or walking her dog.
She also describes experiencing transient episodes of blurred vision and difficulty with balance.
- Cervical spinal stenosis with cervical spondylotic myelopathy
Her past medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia.
- Total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (3 months prior)
- Prednisone 60 mg PO daily (tapering regimen for giant cell arteritis)
Alcohol: Occasional (1-2 glasses of wine per week).
On physical examination, her blood pressure is 150/90 mmHg in the right arm and 130/80 mmHg in the left arm.
Auscultation of the chest is unremarkable, and carotid bruits are absent.
Neurological examination is normal at rest.
Doppler ultrasound of the upper extremities reveals a significant stenosis of the proximal left subclavian artery with reversed flow in the left vertebral artery.

encounters.cc: Three-month history of progressive abdominal bloating and early satiety with unintentional weight loss

lines: Three-month history of progressive abdominal bloating and early satiety with unintentional weight loss

This 70-year-old female with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, coronary artery disease, subclavian steal syndrome, and giant cell arteritis on prednisone taper presents with three-month progressive abdominal bloating and early satiety.
She has also unintentionally lost 4 kg (9 lbs) over the past 2 months.
She denies nausea, vomiting, constipation, or vaginal bleeding.
- Cervical spinal stenosis with cervical spondylotic myelopathy
Her medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia,.
Surgical history includes a cholecystectomy and appendectomy in her 40s.
She takes managed with amlodipine and atorvastatin.
- Prednisone 60 mg PO daily (tapering regimen for giant cell arteritis)
Family history is notable for her mother dying of “stomach problems” in her 60s and a sister recently diagnosed with breast cancer.
Alcohol: Occasional (1-2 glasses of wine per week).
On examination, her abdomen is mildly distended with shifting dullness and a fluid wave.
There is no palpable adnexal mass on bimanual exam,
Pelvic ultrasound reveals bilateral complex adnexal masses with solid and cystic components and moderate free fluid in the abdomen.
Biopsy reveals papillary structures with concentric calcifications.
She is referred for diagnostic laparoscopy,

encounters.cc: Two-week history of persistent temporal headache with recent transient vision loss in the right eye

lines: Two-week history of persistent temporal headache with recent transient vision loss in the right eye
This 70-year-old female with giant cell arteritis on prednisone taper presents with two-week temporal headache.
She describes throbbing pain rated 7 out of 10 in intensity.
She reports tenderness when combing her hair and expresses concern about a recent episode of transient vision loss in the right eye that resolved within a few minutes.
- Cervical spinal stenosis with cervical spondylotic myelopathy
She has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia.
- Total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (3 months prior)
- Prednisone 60 mg PO daily (tapering regimen for giant cell arteritis)
Alcohol: Occasional (1-2 glasses of wine per week).
On physical examination, her temporal arteries appear prominent and are tender to palpation.
Her jaw becomes fatigued while chewing.

encounters.cc: Two-day history of altered mental status with confusion, agitation, and visual hallucinations

lines: Two-day history of altered mental status with confusion, agitation, and visual hallucinations
This patient with major depressive disorder returns to the emergency department.
Her daughter reports that the patient has been increasingly confused over the past two days, with episodes of agitation and visual hallucinations.
- Giant cell arteritis or autoimmune inflammatory condition (diagnosed 2022-09-15)
- Cervical spinal stenosis with cervical spondylotic myelopathy
- Total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (3 months prior)
The patient's medications include amitriptyline and hydrochlorothiazide.
- Prednisone 60 mg PO daily (tapering regimen for giant cell arteritis)
Alcohol: Occasional (1-2 glasses of wine per week).
Heart rate of 110 bpm, blood pressure of 145/90 mmHg, and a temperature of 37.2°C (99°F)
On examination, the patient is disoriented to time and place.
She has dry mucous membranes, dilated pupils that are slow to react to light, and flushed skin.
Bowel sounds are hypoactive, and she is unable to void on command.
An electrocardiogram (ECG) is performed, showing a QRS duration of 120 ms and a QTc interval of 500 ms.
